title: What is known about 1RB1LC_1LC1RD_1LA0LB_0RB1RE_1RF0RA_---0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LC_1LC1RD_1LA0LB_0RB1RE_1RF0RA_---0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is mostly two blocks: an alternating block (10)^x followed by a solid block 1^y. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) finds no halt in the first 1015 steps.

What Lean proves. The whole frame map: 6 tape shapes, 30 cases, each proved for all sizes by a symbolic run (next_sound), and the cases where the map is undefined halt (none_halts). So the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the map, iterated from the frame the run reaches after 1 steps, reaches one of those cases (halts_iff). By native_decide the first 108 frames (about 5.95·1011 machine steps) do not. Whether the orbit ever does is open.

The rules in Lean. The wiki's recursion on the tapes A(a, b) is proved for all sizes from the frame map, so the machine halts if and only if the rules lead from A(2, 9) to some A(a, 3) (halts_iff_rules); by native_decide not in the first 108 visits (about 6.8·1023 machine steps). Iterated in C, the rules give no halt in the first 3·1012 visits (about 1.8·1037 steps). No congruence excludes the halt, and the orbit looks random: in that model it halts with probability 1, but only after many more decades.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,959 cells have been visited and 2,754 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.333). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.326).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) runs 1015 steps without a halt. The macro simulator cuts the tape into blocks of K cells, run-length codes them, and crosses a whole run at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with; it agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun cell for cell.

claims.title: Doubling at the left end
claims.text: At the moments the head reaches a new cell on the left between steps 9.85·107 and 9.99·107, the tape is (10)^x 1^y with x = 85, 173, 349, 701 and y falling by the same amounts.

claims.title: The halting state, seen from the run
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps state F was entered 30,382 times, always reading a 1 (F0 halts).

claims.title: The frame map agrees with the machine on a grid
claims.text: For each of the 6 frames and every canonical choice of sizes below 20, the machine reaches exactly the frame, sizes and step count the fitted map predicts (31,259 frames, py/framemap.py verify 20). The map is now proved in Lean; this check is how it was found.

claims.title: The frame map agrees with the run
claims.text: Run from blank tape next to the machine, the fitted map predicts the whole tape at each of the 41,118 frames in the first 5·106 steps (py/framemap.py real 5000000).

claims.title: The whole frame map
claims.text: next in lean/Phases.lean sends each of the 6 frames to the next one the machine reaches, in 30 cases; next_sound proves every case for all parameters, each from a symbolic run in lean/Pieces.lean (generated by py/pieces.py) glued by tape_eq. Where next is undefined (.b l j 2, .d l 0 1, .d l 1 0) the machine halts (none_halts).

claims.title: Halts if and only if the map reaches an undefined case
claims.text: init_start: the run from blank tape reaches Ph.e 1 0 after 1 steps. halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of next from there is a frame where next is none.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> frames
claims.text: no_halt_phases, by native_decide: the first 108 iterates are defined. By the step counts of the fitted map (py/framemap.py run 100000000) that is about 5.95·1011 machine steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.65·10<sup>22</sup> steps (accelerated run, blocks of 4)
claims.text: The run-length simulator tools/c/rleaccel.cpp (blocks of 4 cells, runs of a block crossed in one step, and cycle jumps, each used only after its one-cycle rule has been proved symbolically for all lengths above the minimums it needs; tested cell for cell against direct runs) runs 1,542,400,000 macro steps from blank tape without a halt, in 600 seconds. That is more than 2.65·1022 machine steps. It found no rule that repeats forever, so it does not decide the machine.

claims.title: The wiki's rules on A(a, b), for all sizes
claims.text: Each of the eight rules (start, three growing rules, two restarts, swap, short) is proved as a run of the frame map from the frame of A(a, b) to the frame of its target, for all sizes: a zigzag of b/a frames (loop_ba), for the growing rules a sweep of d/c frames (loop_cd), and single cases of next. op_step gathers them; the domain dom (a ≥ 1, b ≥ 2, not A(1, 2), A(1, 3), A(2, 2), A(3, 2)) is kept by every rule. Step counts are not part of these statements.

claims.title: Halts if and only if the rules reach b = 3
claims.text: halts_iff_rules: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of the wiki's map op from (2, 9) is a pair (a, 3).

claims.title: No b = 3 in the first 10<sup>8</sup> visits
claims.text: no_b3, by native_decide: the first 108 iterates of op from (2, 9) have b ≠ 3. By the rules' step counts (checked in py/rules.py) that is about 6.8·1023 machine steps.

claims.title: a + b is a clock
claims.text: op_sum: every rule adds at least 2 to a + b; orbit_sum: after k visits a + b ≥ 2k + 11. (In the run the growing rules add exactly 3, the swap 4, so a + b ≈ 3.5 per visit.)

claims.title: No halt in the first 3·10<sup>12</sup> visits (about 1.8·10<sup>37</sup> steps)
claims.text: c/abrun.c iterates the rules from A(2, 9) in 128-bit integers with their exact step counts: 3·1012 visits without b = 3, ending at A(6583418669566, 3916580488195); that is 18,374,996,873,246,197,841,670,520,444,117,981,496 ≈ 1.8·1037 machine steps. Of its 41 logged visits with 1 ≤ b − a ≤ 8, none has a even and b − a = 4. tools/collatz/c/amap.c agrees over the first 1012 visits. The steps grow like 0.68 N3 in the number N of visits.
claims.where: gcc -O2 -o abrun c/abrun.c && ./abrun 3000000000000 10000000000 (about 7 hours; resumable from any logged prog line)

claims.title: No congruence invariant excludes b = 3
claims.text: The halt needs a visit A(a, a + 4) with a even. Over the visits with b > a and b − a ≤ 10<sup>6</sup> among the first 3·10<sup>9</sup>, the residues (a mod M, (b − a) mod M) are far from uniform, yet for every M tried (2<sup>k</sup> up to 256; 48, 90, 120, 210, 252) the classes with a even and b − a ≡ 4 get the same share as any other even residue. The rules applied to residues mod every even M up to 128 also reach them.

claims.title: A doubling map in disguise
claims.text: With s = a + b as the clock, the swap is a ↦ 2a − s + 1 and the growing rules a ↦ 2a + 4 or 2a + 3: x = a/s follows x ↦ 2x mod 1 up to O(1/s). The swap/grow digits are its binary expansion; their blocks of 12 are equidistributed over the first 10<sup>9</sup> visits (chi-square 3,956 on 4,095 degrees of freedom). The halt asks for one exact point of this map.

claims.title: The halting visit looks like a rare random event
claims.text: Visits with a even and b − a = g, for each small even g, come about 0.11 times per decade of visit index, steadily from 105 to 1010 and flat in g (c/abstat.c). For g = 4 that predicts about 1.3 halts in the 12 decades run, so none is unremarkable. Of 9,000 orbits from random A(a, b) with a, b < 109, run 106 visits each, 5 halt by this rule (c/abrand.c; for example A(264421744, 92483937) reaches A(358606020, 3) after 485,721 visits). In that model the run halts with probability 1, with a median of about 2·1018 visits (about 1055 steps).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Its tape is an alternating block followed by a solid block; at the left end the alternating block about doubles again and again, eating into the solid block, until the solid block is used up and a new round starts.

facts.text: No halt in the first 3·10<sup>12</sup> visits of the wiki's rules.
The wiki's rules are proved in Lean: it halts if and only if they lead from A(2, 9) to some A(a, 3). Not in the first 108 visits (native_decide).
No halt in the run-length accelerator (proved cycle jumps, blocks of 4).
No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> frames of the frame map proved in Lean (about 5.95·10<sup>11</sup> machine steps).
It halts if and only if the frame map, iterated from the first frame, reaches a frame where it is undefined.
No halt in an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells).
The alternating block doubles at the expense of the solid block.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the C simulator; 3,959 cells visited.

sections.heading: What the machine does
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell on the left. With a for 10, around step 9.85·107:

Each time, the alternating block goes from x to 2x + 3 (85, 173, 349, 701) and the solid block loses the same number of cells (1663 − 173 = 1490, 1490 − 349 = 1141, 1141 − 701 = 440). Rewriting a block of length x costs about x passes of length x, so the step count between left growths grows like the square of the width (61,683, 247,275 and 990,171 steps here), and the width grows like the cube root of the step count. When the solid block runs out a new round starts. This is the same doubling seen in the three machines 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_…_1RF0LD_---0RE, with different states.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The halting transition is F reading a 0. F is entered only from E reading a 0 (1RF), so a halt needs E>0 0: E on a 0 with another 0 just to its right. In the first 108 steps F was entered 30,382 times, every time on a 1, and 30,101 of those times at least 7 cells from the left end.

Whether the end of a round can leave E in front of two 0s is open. In the related machines 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_…_1RF0LD_---0RE the halt can only come at the moment the tape is all 1s, and only for a sparse list of tape lengths; whether the same holds here has not been checked.

sections.heading: The frame map in Lean
html: The frames (blank tape outside; X is the head in state X on the next cell; u^v is v copies of u, so 11^L is 2L ones; a frame counts only at a moment where the head turns round):

• b: 1^L B 10 10^j 1^R
  • a: 1^L 10^j 110 A 1^R
  • c: 1^L 0 C 0 10^j 1^R
  • d: 1^L A 01 10^j 1^R
  • e: 1^L 10^j B
  • f: 1^L 10^j 1101 B
The map next (Lean names; each variable a natural number):

The map was found by fitting the machine's runs (py/framemap.py) and collapsing the fit into cases (py/pieces.py); Lean then checks every case for all sizes. It is undefined only at .b l j 2, .d l 0 1, .d l 1 0, and those halt. So the open question is exactly whether the orbit of Ph.e 1 0 reaches one of them; the first 108 frames do not.

sections.heading: Exact tapes, exact step counts
html:
The bbchallenge wiki page of this machine (analysis by Racheline) writes its recursion the way the wiki writes Antihydra's: one family of tapes, then rules. Here each rule also has the exact number of machine steps it takes. A visit is any moment at which the tape has the form

A(a, b) := 0∞ 1a 0 C> 1b 0∞ (a ≥ 1)

The Lean map of the section above is finer: A(a, b) is the Lean frame b(a − 2, 1, b − 1) three steps earlier (for a = 1, the frame d(0, 2, b − 1) five steps earlier), so each rule below is the run of Lean cases from one such frame to the next: mostly a zigzag of b and a frames (2j + 5 and 2j + 4 steps each) and a sweep of d and c frames (5 and 1 steps each).

rulefrom → tostepswhen
start0∞ A> 0∞ → A(2, 9)52
growA(a, b) → A(2a + 4, b − a − 1)2a2 + 12a − 1a even, b ≥ a + 3
growA(a, b) → A(2a + 3, b − a)2a2 + 12a + 13a odd, b ≥ a + 4
grow, b runs outA(a, a + 3) → A(2a + 1, 9)2a2 + 12a + 39a odd
restartA(a, a + 2) → A(1, 2a + 7)2a2 + 9a + 23a ≥ 2
restartA(a, a + 1) → A(4, 2a + 4)2a2 + 5a + 7a ≥ 3
swapA(a, b) → A(a − b + 1, 2b + 3)2b2 + b + 5a ≥ b ≥ 4
shortA(a, 2) → A(a − 3, 7)25a ≥ 4
haltA(a, 3) → halt11a ≥ 2; F reads 0

The rules and their targets are the wiki's; the step counts and the bounds on a are added here (the wiki states the rules without them). The four tapes A(1, 2), A(1, 3), A(2, 2) and A(3, 2) are outside every rule, and no rule leads to them, nor to b ≤ 1.

The rules themselves are now proved in Lean for all sizes (lean/Rules.lean, next section). Below them is the frame map they are made of: every case of next for all sizes (next_sound in lean/Phases.lean), with the step count of each case in the statement of its piece theorem in lean/Pieces.lean (next_sound itself only says that some number of steps exists), the halts (none_halts; the halt row is .b l j 2) and halts_iff. python3 py/rules.py checks each row three ways: direct simulation from 3,418 tapes A(a, b) (a, b < 60) to the next visit or the halt, giving the target and the step count of the table; the Lean cases from the frame of A(a, b) to the next such frame, giving the same; and the run from blank tape, where the 238 visits of the first 107 steps are exactly the rules' orbit from A(2, 9) with the same step counts, and the same as the Lean map's frames. The Lean map followed for 5·105 frames (2.1·108 steps, 685 visits) agrees with the rules too. Lean now proves that the rules hold for all sizes, so the machine halts iff they lead from A(2, 9) to some A(a, 3).

For example A(1, 7) = 1 0 C> 17: A(5, 6) after 27 steps, A(4, 14) after 82, A(12, 9) after 79, A(4, 21) after 176, A(12, 16) after 79, A(28, 3) after 431, and the halt 11 steps later: 885 steps in all, which is what direct simulation gives.

sections.heading: Looking for an invariant that excludes the halt
html: lean/Rules.lean proves each rule above for all sizes from the frame map (a zigzag of b/a frames, a sweep of d/c frames, a few single cases), and with it halts_iff_rules: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the rules lead from A(2, 9) to some A(a, 3). The only rule that can give b = 3 is the growing rule from A(a, a + 4) with a even. So the whole question is whether the orbit ever lands exactly on that diagonal.

Following the orbit is cheap: one visit is a few integer operations, while the sizes grow only about linearly in the number of visits. no_b3 checks the first 108 visits in Lean (about 6.8·1023 machine steps), and C runs the first 3·1012 (c/abrun.c; about 1.8·1037 steps, a and b near 1013). Half the visits are swaps and almost all the rest growing rules; restarts are rare (8 in the first 107 visits).

Why it looks random. Every rule adds a fixed amount to s = a + b (3 for a growing rule, 4 for a swap; proved in Lean as op_sum), so s is a clock, about 3.5 per visit. Measured against it, the swap is a ↦ 2a − s + 1 and the growing rules are a ↦ 2a + 4 or 2a + 3: the ratio x = a/s just doubles mod 1, the binary shift, with a little noise from the +3s and +4s. The sequence of swaps and growths is the binary expansion of x, and its blocks of 12 digits come out equidistributed. A halt needs the orbit to land on one exact point, a = (s − 4)/2 with a even, which is the same kind of question as whether a Collatz orbit ever hits a given number.

No congruence does it. The residues of a and b − a at the visits are far from uniform (when a is 2 or 3 mod 4, b is always odd), but for every modulus tried, the classes with a even and b − a ≡ 4 get their full share of visits, and the rules applied to residues reach them too.

The halting visit looks like a rare random event. For each small even g, visits with a even and b − a = g come about 0.11 times per decade of the visit index, steadily from 105 to 1010. For g = 4 that predicts about 1.3 halts so far, so having seen none says little. Orbits from random starts of size 109 do halt by this rule (5 of 9,000 within 106 visits; for example A(264421744, 92483937) after 485,721 visits). If the orbit behaves like a random one, it halts with probability 1, but the median wait is about 2·1018 visits, about 1055 machine steps, beyond any direct run. Proving that it never halts would need an argument that the visits always miss one exact diagonal, and nothing of that kind is in sight.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.333). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.326).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,959 cells (1,403 left of the start, 1,816 right), with a density of 1s of 0.696.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: doubling between an alternating and a solid block
summary: Its tape is an alternating block followed by a solid block; at the left end the alternating block about doubles again and again, eating into the solid block, until the solid block is used up and a new round starts. The wiki's rules are proved in Lean (halts iff they reach b = 3); no halt in 1.8e37 steps by the rules; no congruence rules the halt out.
